answer: Each identity locks an 80-credit bond and posts an orchard ledger of inputs, outputs, and fees. An ember seal binds it to one key; one seal cannot certify two ledgers. At a terrace checkpoint, any auditor recomputes the totals; a mismatch or duplicate seal burns the bond, 40 percent to the auditor. Shared funding is visible, so the k-th identity from one source pays 15+5(k-1): the 1000th pays 5010; 1000 fakes pay 2512500 plus 80000 at risk. Copied ledgers fail: seal and history mismatch the clone. An honest identity pays one bond and 15, and keeps the bond after an audit.
